input_messages.content: Hello, I’m having trouble sending picture messages from my phone. It’s been a few hours now and I just can’t seem to get them to go through. Can you help me fix this?
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. I hope that’s enough to get started.

I just checked, and it looks like my phone can’t send picture messages right now. Also, I’m not connected to Wi-Fi at the moment. 

I’m not sure about browsing the internet when I’m not on Wi-Fi—should I try that, or is there something else I should check?
Oh, I just noticed that my phone shows an airplane icon at the top. Does that mean airplane mode is on? Could that be why I can’t use the internet or send picture messages?
Okay, I’ve turned off Airplane Mode. Now I see some bars at the top and it says “2G.” Should I try sending a picture message again, or do you want me to check if I can browse the internet first?
I changed the network mode to prefer 4G and 5G, and now the top of my phone shows “5G” with full bars. Should I try sending a picture message again now, or do you want me to check the internet first?

I tried sending a picture message again, but it still won’t go through. This is getting a bit frustrating. Should I check if I can browse the internet now, or is there something else I should do first?
I tried to check the internet on my phone, but it looks like there’s no connection at all. I couldn’t open any websites or use anything that needs the internet. What should I do next?

I checked my APN settings, and it looks like there’s something called “internet” listed, but I don’t see anything set for the MMSC URL. Is that a problem? Should I go ahead and reset the APN settings, or do you want me to do something else?

I’ve reset the APN settings like you said, but it says the changes will only take effect after I restart my phone. I’m a bit nervous about rebooting—will I lose any of my photos or messages if I do this?
I restarted my phone, but I still can’t send picture messages, and the internet isn’t working either. Is there anything else I can try? This is starting to worry me a bit.
I checked, and my SIM card is showing as active and working. What should I do next?
Oh, I see. I didn’t realize I’d gone over my data limit. Let’s go ahead and add 2GB of data, please. Can you confirm the total cost before you do anything? I just want to make sure I understand.
Yes, please go ahead and add the 2GB for $4.00. I’d really like to get my picture messages working again. Let me know when it’s done and if I need to do anything else!
I restarted my phone again, and now it looks like I can send picture messages! Thank you so much for your help. I really appreciate your patience with me. I think everything is working now.
Thank you! I really appreciate your help today. Have a wonderful day yourself! ###STOP###

user_scenario.persona:
At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

Hello, I’m having trouble sending picture messages from my phone. It’s been a few hours now and I just can’t seem to get them to go through. Can you help me fix this?

Thank you for reaching out about your issue with sending picture messages (MMS). I can help you troubleshoot and resolve this problem.

To get started, I’ll need to identify your account. Could you please provide one of the following:
- The phone number associated with your account,
- Your full name and date of birth (in YYYY-MM-DD format), or
- Your customer ID (if you have it)?

Once I have this information, I can begin assisting you further.
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. I hope that’s enough to get started.

Thank you for providing your information, John. I have identified your account.

To help you with sending picture messages (MMS), I’ll need to ask a few questions and may guide you through some steps on your phone. Could you please confirm:
- Are you able to send regular text messages (SMS) without any issues?
- Are you able to use mobile data (browse the internet) when not connected to Wi-Fi?

This will help me determine if the issue is specific to MMS or related to your overall network or data connection.
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.
Wi-Fi is turned OFF.

I just checked, and it looks like my phone can’t send picture messages right now. Also, I’m not connected to Wi-Fi at the moment. 

I’m not sure about browsing the internet when I’m not on Wi-Fi—should I try that, or is there something else I should check?

Yes, please try browsing the internet on your phone using mobile data (not Wi-Fi). For example, try opening a website in your browser.

Let me know if you are able to access the internet using mobile data. This will help determine if the issue is with your mobile data connection, which is required for sending picture messages (MMS).
Status Bar: ✈️ Airplane Mode | 🔋 80%
Oh, I just noticed that my phone shows an airplane icon at the top. Does that mean airplane mode is on? Could that be why I can’t use the internet or send picture messages?

Yes, the airplane icon means that Airplane Mode is enabled on your phone. When Airplane Mode is on, all wireless communications—including cellular service and mobile data—are turned off. This would prevent you from sending picture messages and using the internet.

Please turn off Airplane Mode on your phone. Once it’s off, wait a few moments for your phone to reconnect to the network, then try sending a picture message again and see if you can browse the internet.

Let me know if this resolves the issue or if you need further assistance.

Airplane Mode is now OFF.
Status Bar: 📶¹ Poor | 2G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Okay, I’ve turned off Airplane Mode. Now I see some bars at the top and it says “2G.” Should I try sending a picture message again, or do you want me to check if I can browse the internet first?

Thank you for the update. Since your phone is now showing “2G,” this network type is generally not suitable for sending picture messages (MMS) or for reliable internet browsing.

Let’s improve your connection by switching your phone’s network mode to prefer 4G or 5G, which will provide better data speeds and support MMS.

Please change your phone’s network mode to “4G/5G preferred” if possible. If you need instructions on how to do this, let me know your phone model and I can guide you through the steps.

After changing the network mode, wait a moment for your phone to reconnect, then try sending a picture message and browsing the internet again. Let me know how it goes!

Preferred Network Mode set to: 4g_5g_preferred
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
I changed the network mode to prefer 4G and 5G, and now the top of my phone shows “5G” with full bars. Should I try sending a picture message again now, or do you want me to check the internet first?

That’s great! Now that your phone is connected to 5G with full signal, please try sending a picture message again.

If it still doesn’t work, also check if you can browse the internet using mobile data (not Wi-Fi). Let me know the results for both—this will help confirm if the issue is resolved or if further troubleshooting is needed.
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.

I tried sending a picture message again, but it still won’t go through. This is getting a bit frustrating. Should I check if I can browse the internet now, or is there something else I should do first?

Thank you for your patience, and I understand this is frustrating. Yes, please check if you can browse the internet using mobile data (not Wi-Fi). This will help determine if the issue is with your mobile data connection or specifically with MMS.

Let me know if you are able to access websites or use apps that require internet access. Based on your results, I’ll guide you through the next steps to resolve the issue.
Speed test failed: No Connection.
I tried to check the internet on my phone, but it looks like there’s no connection at all. I couldn’t open any websites or use anything that needs the internet. What should I do next?

Thank you for checking. Since you have no internet connection on mobile data, this could be affecting your ability to send picture messages.

Let’s check your phone’s APN (Access Point Name) settings, as incorrect APN settings are a common cause of mobile data and MMS issues. Please check your APN settings on your phone and let me know if you see anything unusual, or if you’d like, I can guide you through resetting your APN settings to default.

Would you like instructions on how to reset your APN settings?

Current APN Name: internet
MMSC URL (for picture messages): Not Set
(These are technical settings, usually best left unchanged.)

I checked my APN settings, and it looks like there’s something called “internet” listed, but I don’t see anything set for the MMSC URL. Is that a problem? Should I go ahead and reset the APN settings, or do you want me to do something else?

Yes, the missing MMSC URL in your APN settings is likely the reason you can’t send picture messages (MMS) and have no mobile data connection. Resetting your APN settings to default should restore the correct values, including the MMSC URL.

Please go ahead and reset your APN settings to default on your phone. After resetting, you’ll need to reboot (restart) your device for the changes to take effect.

Once you’ve done both steps, try sending a picture message and browsing the internet again. Let me know if this resolves the issue or if you need further assistance.

APN settings will reset at reboot.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%

I’ve reset the APN settings like you said, but it says the changes will only take effect after I restart my phone. I’m a bit nervous about rebooting—will I lose any of my photos or messages if I do this?

You will not lose any of your photos, messages, or personal data by rebooting (restarting) your phone. Restarting simply turns your phone off and back on, which helps apply the new APN settings.

It’s safe to proceed. Please restart your phone now, and after it powers back on, try sending a picture message and browsing the internet again. Let me know how it goes or if you need any more help.

Resetting APN settings...
Restarting network services...
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.
Speed test failed: No Connection.
I restarted my phone, but I still can’t send picture messages, and the internet isn’t working either. Is there anything else I can try? This is starting to worry me a bit.

Thank you for letting me know. I understand this is concerning, and I’m here to help you through it.

Let’s check the status of your SIM card next, as SIM issues can also cause loss of service and data. Please check your SIM card status in your phone’s settings and let me know if it shows as “Active,” “Missing,” or “Locked.” If you need instructions on how to check this, let me know your phone model and I can guide you.

Once you provide the SIM status, I’ll advise you on the next steps.
Your SIM card is active and working.
I checked, and my SIM card is showing as active and working. What should I do next?

Thank you for confirming that your SIM card is active. Since your SIM is working, your APN settings have been reset, and you’re connected to 5G with full bars but still have no mobile data or MMS, I’ll check your account and line status for any issues that could be affecting your service.

Please hold on while I review your line status.
